mainTopic: Whether gold or silver counts as currency (טבעא) or commodity (פירא): proofs from the משנה, רבי חייא, a ברייתא of coin values, and the בית שמאי–בית הלל dispute on redeeming onto gold
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining רבי's later view: silver, which everyone accepts, is currency, and gold is a commodity. רב אשי argues that רבי's earlier view (gold is currency) fits the משנה's line 'copper acquires silver' better. The גמרא rejects this, because that line is needed anyway: in some places copper is used more than silver. Next, a story about רב repaying gold דינרים to רבי חייא's daughter seems to prove that gold is currency. That proof is also pushed away, since רב owned dinars of his own. רבא then proves from a ברייתא of coin values that its תנא treats gold as currency, because it measures the fixed פדיון הבן payment in gold. Finally, the גמרא brings the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל about turning holy silver into gold. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue over whether that dispute also covers redeeming produce onto gold. The amud ends as the גמרא begins to show which of them holds which view.

steps.title: Silver is currency and gold is a commodity in רבי's later view
steps.stepSummary: Finishing רבי's later view: silver coins, which circulate easily, are currency. Gold coins, which do not, are a commodity. Taking the commodity acquires the currency.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Silver,] which circulates, is currency. Gold, which does not circulate, is a commodity. And taking the commodity acquires the currency.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a sentence that began on the previous page. It explains why רבי, in his old age, ruled that gold acquires silver.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What decides the question here is how easily a coin is accepted, not how much it is worth. Silver is accepted by everyone, so it counts as currency. Gold is harder to spend, so it counts as a commodity, and taking the commodity (gold) completes the deal for the currency (silver).

keyTerms.meaning: currency (a coin that works as money)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that the more valuable coin is automatically the currency. In רבי's later view, the coin that is easier to spend (silver) is the currency, even though gold is worth more.

phrases.english: [Silver,] which circulates, is currency.
phrases.notes: The word for silver is at the end of the previous page. This is רבי's reasoning from his old age.

phrases.english: Gold, which does not circulate, is a commodity,
and the commodity acquires the currency.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the explanation of רבי's old-age ruling that was begun on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי's later view, silver (which circulates) is currency and gold is a commodity, so taking gold acquires silver.

steps.title: רב אשי prefers רבי's earlier view
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says רבי's earlier view, that gold is currency compared to silver, is more reasonable. His evidence is the line in the משנה that copper acquires silver.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It is more reasonable to follow what רבי taught in his youth, since the משנה teaches: 'Copper acquires silver.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי states his position and points to the line in the משנה he will use as evidence. The next step explains how that line proves his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his youth, רבי held that gold, being more valuable, is currency, and silver is a commodity compared to gold. רב אשי thinks the משנה's copper-and-silver ruling fits that earlier view better. Here he only names the source; the argument comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: like (what he taught in) his youth
it is reasonable / it makes sense

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
It is reasonable [to follow] his youth,
phrases.notes: He means רבי's earlier teaching: gold is currency and silver is a commodity.

phrases.english: since [the משנה] teaches:
"Copper acquires silver."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the later view is explained, רב אשי argues in favor of the earlier view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי's earlier view (gold is currency compared to silver) is more reasonable.

steps.title: Why the copper ruling supports the earlier view
steps.stepSummary: If silver is a commodity compared to gold, the משנה has something new to teach: silver is still currency compared to copper. If silver is already currency even compared to gold, then saying it is currency compared to copper would be obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works if you say silver is a commodity compared to gold. That is why the משנה teaches 'copper acquires silver': although silver is a commodity compared to gold, it is currency compared to copper. But if you say silver is currency even compared to gold, which is worth more than it, then compared to copper, which silver beats in both value and ease of spending, does the משנה need to say it?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי spells out his proof. A line in the משנה should teach something new, and only the earlier view leaves something new for this line to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the earlier view, silver is 'commodity' compared to gold, so it is a real חידוש that silver becomes 'currency' compared to copper. Under the later view, silver already counts as currency even against the more valuable gold. So it would obviously be currency against copper, which is weaker in both value and ease of spending, and the line would be unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: is it necessary? (it should be obvious)

steps.whyThisMatters: This uses a common גמרא principle: a משנה does not state the obvious. A reading under which a line teaches nothing new is considered weaker.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
silver, compared to gold, is a commodity,
that is why it teaches:
"Copper acquires silver,"

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל פִּי דִּלְגַבֵּי דַּהֲבָא פֵּירָא הָוֵיא,
phrases.english: that even though, compared to gold, it is a commodity,
compared to copper, it is currency.
But if you say
silver, compared to gold, is currency,
now, if compared to gold, which is more valuable than it,
you say it is currency,
then compared to copper,
where it is more valuable and it circulates more, is it necessary [to say]?
phrases.notes: 'It' here is the silver, which beats copper in both value and ease of spending.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the משנה line cited in step 2 supports רבי's earlier view.
steps.raayaObject: רבי's earlier view, that silver is a commodity compared to gold.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that copper acquires silver, which would be unnecessary under the later view.

steps.title: The copper ruling is needed even under the later view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב אשי's proof. Under the later view, the copper ruling still teaches something: even where copper coins are spent more easily than silver, copper is still a commodity, because in some places copper is not accepted at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary. You might have thought: in a place where these copper coins are commonly used, they circulate more easily than silver, so say they are currency! The משנה teaches us that since there is a place where they are not accepted, they are a commodity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב אשי. Even under רבי's later view, the line 'copper acquires silver' is not obvious, because it teaches something new about copper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי assumed silver always beats copper in ease of spending, but in some places copper is actually used more. The משנה teaches that what counts is whether a coin is accepted everywhere. Silver is, and copper is not. So the proof falls away, and the later view still stands.
steps.whatToRemember: Under רבי's later view, a coin counts as currency only if it is accepted everywhere. Copper is a commodity even where it is popular, because some places do not accept it. רב אשי's proof for the earlier view is rejected.

phrases.english: It was necessary,
it would have entered your mind to say:
these copper coins, in a place where they are commonly used,
they circulate more than silver,
so say they are currency!
It teaches us,
since there is a place
where they are not used, they are a commodity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אשי's proof by showing the copper ruling teaches something new even under רבי's later view.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only. It does not show that the earlier view is wrong, just that this משנה cannot decide between the views.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב אשי assumed silver always circulates better than copper. In some places copper circulates better, so the משנה needed to teach that copper is still a commodity.

steps.title: רבי חייא tells רב to repay gold coins by count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא claims רבי חייא also holds that gold is currency. It brings the story of רב borrowing gold דינרים from רבי חייא's daughter. The coins went up in value, and רבי חייא told רב to repay the same coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא also holds gold is currency. רב borrowed gold dinars from רבי חייא's daughter, and later the dinars went up in value. He asked רבי חייא, who told him: go pay her back good, full-weight dinars.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to show that רבי חייא agrees with the view that gold is currency. The logic of the proof is spelled out in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב worried that giving back coins now worth more would count as paying extra, which looks like רבית. רבי חייא said to return the same number of dinars and not worry about their value. Ignoring the change in value like this suggests he treated the gold dinars as money, not as merchandise.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin, meaning currency (as opposed to merchandise)
Went up in value, became more expensive

steps.confusionAlert: The דינרים here are gold. The whole proof depends on gold being the thing that changed in value.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiyya too holds
that gold is currency.
For Rav borrowed dinars
from the daughter of Rabbi Chiyya;
in the end, the dinars went up in value.
He came before Rabbi Chiyya;
he said to him: Go, pay her back
good, full-weight ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַבִּי חִיָּיא סְבַר דַּהֲבָא טִבְעָא הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב אשי's proof was rejected, the גמרא opens a new proof that gold is currency, this time from a story.
steps.raayaObject: That gold is currency compared to silver (רבי's earlier view)
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא's ruling to רב about repaying gold dinars that rose in value

steps.title: Why the ruling only makes sense if gold is currency
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the proof. If gold is currency, returning the same coins is fine. If gold is a commodity, this would be like borrowing a סאה of produce and returning a סאה, which is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If gold is currency, the ruling works well. But if gold is a commodity, this is a case of a סאה for a סאה, which is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out why רבי חייא's ruling proves that he holds gold is currency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money is the measure of value, so returning the same number of coins is a normal repayment. Merchandise can rise in price, and lending merchandise to be returned in kind is forbidden as סאה בסאה. Since רבי חייא allowed it, he must have treated gold as currency.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'fruit'; here it means a commodity, merchandise
Lending a סאה of produce to be paid back with a סאה; forbidden because of רבית

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
that gold is currency, it is fine.
But if you say it is a commodity,
it is a se'ah for a se'ah, which is forbidden!
phrases.notes: Lending produce to be returned in kind is forbidden, since its price might rise and the lender would get back more. That counts as רבית.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא דַּהֲבָא טִבְעָא הָוֵי – שַׁפִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the logic of the proof from the story in Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי חייא held gold is currency
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ban on סאה בסאה would forbid his ruling if gold were a commodity

steps.title: רב already owned dinars, so the loan was allowed anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes away the proof. רב had dinars of his own elsewhere. A borrower who already owns the item is like someone saying 'lend me until my son comes or until I find the key,' and that kind of loan is permitted even with a commodity.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב had dinars. Since he had dinars, it is as if he said to her: Lend me until my son comes, or until I find the key.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from רבי חייא. The ruling can be explained even if gold is a commodity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lending merchandise to be returned in kind is forbidden only when the borrower does not already own that merchandise. Since רב owned dinars and just could not reach them right now, the loan was permitted no matter what. So the story says nothing about whether gold is currency.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof from רבי חייא falls away: רב owned dinars of his own, so the loan was permitted even if gold is a commodity.

phrases.english: Rav had dinars,
and since he had dinars,
it is as if he said to her:
Lend me until my son comes
or until I find the key.
phrases.notes: This is borrowed from a משנה case: someone who owns the item but can't reach it right now may borrow and return it in kind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof made in Steps 5 and 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from רבי חייא's ruling only, not the view that gold is currency itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling is explained by רב already owning dinars, which permits a return-in-kind loan even for a commodity

steps.title: רבא's ברייתא: the פרוטה and the איסר
steps.stepSummary: רבא says a certain תנא holds gold is currency, and brings a ברייתא of coin values. A פרוטה is 1/8 of an Italian איסר, which matters for קידושין. An איסר is 1/24 of a silver דינר, which matters for buying and selling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: this תנא holds gold is currency, as a ברייתא teaches: the פרוטה the חכמים spoke of is one-eighth of an Italian איסר. What difference does it make? For marrying a woman. An איסר is one twenty-fourth of a silver דינר. What difference does it make? For buying and selling.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new proof that gold is currency. He starts quoting a ברייתא that lists coin values one after another, each with its practical use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא builds a ladder of coins from small to large. After each value it asks 'what difference does it make?' and names the area of הלכה where that value matters. The part that matters for the proof about gold comes at the top of the ladder, in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage of the משנה period, whose teaching is quoted
The smallest coin value in halacha
The Italian איסר, a small copper coin
What practical difference does it make?
Marrying a woman (with money worth at least a פרוטה)

phrases.english: Rava said: This tanna holds
that gold is currency,
as it is taught: The peruta that they spoke of
is one-eighth of the Italian issar.
What difference does it make? For betrothing a woman.

phrases.aramaic: אִיסָּר – אֶחָד מֵעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה בְּדִינָר שֶׁל כֶּסֶף.
phrases.english: An issar is one twenty-fourth of a silver dinar.
What difference does it make? For buying and selling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר דַּהֲבָא טִבְעָא הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from רבי חייא was rejected, רבא brings a new source that gold is currency.
steps.raayaObject: That gold is currency compared to silver

steps.title: The silver דינר measured against the gold דינר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a silver דינר is 1/25 of a gold דינר, and this matters for פדיון הבן. This is the line רבא's proof is built on.
steps.simpleTranslation: A silver דינר is one twenty-fifth of a gold דינר. What difference does it make? For redeeming a firstborn son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא. Its last line measures silver by gold, which is the line רבא is relying on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each coin is measured by the next coin up, and at the top of the ladder the silver דינר is measured by the gold דינר. That treats gold as the fixed standard of value, which fits the view that gold is currency compared to silver.

keyTerms.meaning: Redeeming a firstborn son from a כהן with five סלעים

steps.whyThisMatters: This ladder of coin values (פרוטה, איסר, silver דינר, gold דינר) is a standard reference used across many areas of הלכה.

phrases.aramaic: דִּינָר שֶׁל כֶּסֶף – אֶחָד מֵעֶשְׂרִים וַחֲמִשָּׁה
phrases.english: A silver dinar is one twenty-fifth
of a gold dinar.
What difference does it make? For the redemption of the firstborn son.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּינָר שֶׁל כֶּסֶף – אֶחָד מֵעֶשְׂרִים וַחֲמִשָּׁה בְּדִינָר שֶׁל זָהָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in Step 8 with the line about silver and gold.
steps.raayaObject: That gold is currency compared to silver
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא measuring the silver דינר as a fraction of the gold דינר

steps.title: Why the ברייתא shows gold is currency
steps.stepSummary: If gold is currency, it makes sense to measure the silver דינר against it. If gold were a commodity, its value would change, and the פדיון הבן payment would keep shifting.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if gold is currency, because then the תנא is measuring against something with a fixed value. But if gold is a commodity, would the תנא measure against something whose price goes up and down? Then sometimes the כהן would have to give money back, and sometimes the father would have to add more for the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly how the line from Step 9 proves that this תנא holds gold is currency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פדיון הבן is a fixed amount: five סלעים. A תנא would only state its value in gold coins if gold has a steady value. If gold were a commodity whose price moves, a gold דינר would sometimes be worth more and sometimes less than the required amount, so it would be a poor measuring stick.

keyTerms.meaning: Currency, a coin with a fixed value
Literally 'fruit'; here, a commodity whose price goes up and down
Something with a fixed, set value
Which gets more expensive and cheaper
The כהן, who receives the פדיון הבן money

phrases.english: It works well if you say it is currency:
the תנא measures by something with a fixed value!
phrases.notes: That 'something' is the gold דינר, the coin the ברייתא from Step 9 uses as its measuring stick.

phrases.english: But if you say it is a commodity,
would the תנא measure by something that goes up and down in price?
Sometimes the כהן would have to give him back money,
and sometimes he would have to add more for the כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פדיון הבן line in Step 9 proves רבא's claim
steps.raayaObject: A certain תנא holds that gold is currency
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that values a silver דינר as 1/25 of a gold דינר for פדיון הבן

steps.title: Conclusion: this תנא treats gold as currency
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא's תנא holds gold is currency, and confirms it.
steps.simpleTranslation: So learn from this that gold is currency. Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רבא's proof and closes this part of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the proof from רבי חייא, which was pushed away in Step 7, this proof stands. The double 'שמע מינה' means the גמרא fully agrees with the conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; the גמרא accepts a conclusion

steps.whatToRemember: רבא proved that at least one תנא holds gold is currency: the ברייתא uses the gold דינר as a fixed standard for measuring the fixed פדיון הבן payment.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from it: it is currency.
Learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: טִבְעָא הָוֵי. שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The תנא of the coin-value ברייתא holds gold is currency

steps.title: A משנה: may silver coins be exchanged for gold coins?
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in מעשר שני: בית שמאי forbid turning holy silver סלעים into gold דינרים, and בית הלל permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה there: בית שמאי say a person may not turn סלעים into gold דינרים, and בית הלל permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source that deals with the same question of whether gold or silver counts as currency. It sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is money that holds the holiness of מעשר שני, which someone wants to transfer onto gold coins. The משנה gives only the two rulings. The reasons, and how far the dispute reaches, come in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
Silver coins, each worth 4 silver דינרים

phrases.english: We learned there: בית שמאי say:
phrases.notes: 'There' is a משנה in מסכת מעשר שני, about coins that hold the holiness of מעשר שני.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם סְלָעִין דִּינְרֵי זָהָב,
phrases.english: A person may not make סלעים into gold דינרים,
and בית הלל permit it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New source on the same theme of gold versus silver as currency
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי forbid exchanging holy silver סלעים for gold דינרים; בית הלל permit it

steps.title: First view: the dispute is only about silver for gold
steps.stepSummary: One of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש says the dispute is only about silver for gold. בית שמאי hold silver is currency and gold is a commodity. בית הלל hold the reverse. Everyone agrees produce may be redeemed onto gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש disagree. One says: the dispute is about סלעים for דינרים. בית שמאי hold silver is currency and gold is a commodity, and we do not transfer holiness from currency onto a commodity. בית הלל hold silver is a commodity and gold is currency, and we do transfer holiness from a commodity onto currency. But everyone agrees we may redeem produce onto gold דינרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first of two opinions explaining the משנה's dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that holiness may move 'up' onto currency but not 'down' onto a commodity. So the whole dispute depends on which metal is the currency. This view limits the dispute to silver for gold, and says redeeming produce onto gold is permitted by everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: We transfer holiness off one item onto another (redemption)
One said (we are not told which of the two)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two sides. In this view בית שמאי call silver the currency, and בית הלל call gold the currency, which matches the ברייתא from Step 9.

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש disagree:

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: מַחְלוֹקֶת בִּסְלָעִים עַל דִּינָרִין,
phrases.english: One said: the dispute is about סלעים for דינרים,
for בית שמאי hold:
silver is currency and gold is a commodity,
and we do not redeem currency onto a commodity.
And בית הלל hold:
silver is a commodity and gold is currency,
and we do redeem a commodity onto currency.
But produce onto gold דינרים:
everyone agrees we may redeem.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning and scope of the משנה in Step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is only about silver for gold; redeeming produce onto gold is permitted by all

steps.title: Why would בית שמאי allow produce onto gold?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the first view's claim that everyone allows redeeming produce onto gold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question that sets up the next step. If בית שמאי call gold a commodity, how can they allow redeeming produce onto it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There seems to be a contradiction. For בית שמאי gold is a commodity, and holiness may not be moved onto a commodity. Yet this view says they allow produce to be redeemed onto gold.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the last line of Step 13
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why everyone, including בית שמאי, agrees produce may be redeemed onto gold

steps.title: Currency or commodity depends on what you compare it to
steps.stepSummary: Just as בית הלל treat silver as a commodity next to gold but as currency next to produce, בית שמאי treat gold as a commodity next to silver but as currency next to produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is just like silver according to בית הלל. For בית הלל, even though silver is a commodity compared to gold, compared to produce it is currency. So too gold for בית שמאי: even though gold is a commodity compared to silver, compared to produce it is currency.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing that 'currency' and 'commodity' are relative labels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A metal can be a commodity compared to the other metal and still count as currency compared to produce. So בית שמאי can call gold a commodity in the silver-for-gold case and still allow redeeming produce onto gold. The proof is that בית הלל say the same thing about silver.

keyTerms.meaning: It is just like (comparing to a known case)

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches that 'currency' versus 'commodity' is a relationship between two items, not a fixed label on one item.

phrases.english: It is just like silver according to בית הלל.
Silver, according to בית הלל:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּכַסְפָּא לְגַבֵּי דַּהֲבָא פֵּירָא הָוֵי,
phrases.english: even though silver compared to gold is a commodity,
compared to produce it is currency.
So too gold, according to בית שמאי:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּדַהֲבָא לְגַבֵּי כַּסְפָּא פֵּירָא הָוֵי,
phrases.english: even though gold compared to silver is a commodity,
compared to produce it is currency.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Currency status is relative; gold is currency compared to produce even for בית שמאי, just as silver is for בית הלל

steps.title: Second view: the dispute includes produce onto gold
steps.stepSummary: The other of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש says בית שמאי and בית הלל argue even about redeeming produce onto gold דינרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one said: even about produce onto דינרים there is a dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second opinion, which makes the dispute wider than the first view did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this view, בית שמאי treat gold as a commodity even compared to produce, so they forbid redeeming produce onto it. This rejects the 'it's relative' idea of Step 15, at least for בית שמאי.

phrases.english: And one said:
Even about produce onto דינרים there is a dispute.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד אָמַר: אַף בְּפֵירוֹת עַל דִּינָרִין מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree even about redeeming produce onto gold דינרים

steps.title: Then why didn't the משנה use the produce case?
steps.stepSummary: If they argue even about produce, the משנה should have stated the dispute with produce, which is the basic redemption case.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says there is a dispute even about produce onto דינרים: instead of arguing about סלעים for דינרים, let them argue about produce onto דינרים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second view: why would the משנה pick the silver case if the produce case is also in dispute?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Redeeming produce is the normal, basic case of מעשר שני redemption. If the dispute covers it, the משנה would be expected to state the dispute there.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

phrases.english: And according to the one who says:
there is a dispute even about produce onto דינרים,
instead of disagreeing about סלעים for דינרים,
let them disagree about produce onto דינרים!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר: אַף בְּפֵירוֹת עַל דִּינָרִין מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second view from Step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The second view's reading of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the dispute covers the basic produce case, the משנה should have taught it there and not in the silver case

steps.title: The silver case shows how far בית הלל go
steps.stepSummary: Had the משנה used produce, we might think בית הלל agree that gold is a commodity compared to silver. The silver case teaches that בית הלל permit even that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Had they disagreed about produce onto דינרים, I would have thought that applies only to produce onto דינרים. But for סלעים for דינרים, I would have thought בית הלל agree with בית שמאי that gold compared to silver is a commodity, so we may not redeem. So the משנה teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what we learn from the case the משנה chose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The silver case is the bigger חידוש for בית הלל: gold is currency even compared to silver. Had the משנה used the produce case, we might think בית הלל call gold currency only compared to produce. The second view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first assumption)

steps.whatToRemember: Both views agree that for בית הלל gold is currency even compared to silver. They argue only about whether בית שמאי allow redeeming produce onto gold.

phrases.english: Had they disagreed about produce onto דינרים,
I would have thought:
this applies only to produce onto דינרים,
but with סלעים for דינרים,

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדוּ לָהֶן בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי
phrases.english: בית הלל agree with בית שמאי
that gold compared to silver is a commodity
and we do not redeem.
So it teaches us otherwise.
phrases.notes: By using the silver case, the משנה shows that בית הלל permit even this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אִיפְּלוּג בְּפֵירוֹת עַל דִּינָרִין, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the משנה chose this case: it is the bigger חידוש for בית הלל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the משנה had used produce, we would think בית הלל agree that gold is a commodity compared to silver
steps.terutzMaskana: The silver case teaches that בית הלל treat gold as currency even compared to silver

steps.title: Suggesting that רבי יוחנן is the one who forbids redeeming onto gold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that רבי יוחנן is the one who holds the second view: that בית שמאי forbid even redeeming produce onto gold דינרים. It introduces another statement of his to prove it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us conclude that it is רבי יוחנן who said that one may not redeem produce onto gold, because רבי יוחנן said elsewhere:
steps.whatsHappening: Until now we only knew that one of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש said each view. The גמרא is setting up a proof to show which is which; the actual proof, another quote from רבי יוחנן, comes right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, one view said everyone allows redeeming produce onto gold, and the other said even that is disputed, with בית שמאי forbidding it. Here the גמרא suggests that the second view, where 'אין מחללין' applies even to produce according to בית שמאי, belongs to רבי יוחנן. The support will come from a different ruling of רבי יוחנן that fits this position.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let it be concluded'. The גמרא proposes settling a question, usually by bringing a proof.
'We do not redeem'. Here: one may not transfer the holiness of מעשר שני produce onto gold coins.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop at this line thinking the proof is done. This line only makes the suggestion. The quote that proves it comes in the next line.

phrases.english: Conclude that it is רבי יוחנן
phrases.notes: Back in steps 13 and 16 we were only told 'one of them' said each view. Now the גמרא tries to figure out who.

phrases.english: who said: one does not redeem [produce onto gold dinars],
as רבי יוחנן said:

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּסְתַּיֵּים דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הוּא דְּאָמַר אֵין מְחַלְּלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both unnamed opinions have been explained, the גמרא moves on to work out which אמורא holds which opinion.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן is the one who holds produce may not be redeemed onto gold דינרים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A separate statement of רבי יוחנן, introduced here and quoted in the following text.
